question: Which of the following idioms means ‘to steal from a shop’?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"to steal from a shop"** means to take something from a store without paying for it. (दुकान से चोरी करना)

 
 
• **Example: **He was caught trying **to steal from a shop,** which is a criminal offense.
 
 
 
• **Five-finger discount** is a slang term for shoplifting or stealing items from a store. (दुकान से चोरी करना)
 
 
• **Example: **She was caught taking a** five-finger discount** at the local supermarket.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the idiom **'to steal from a shop' **is **'Five-finger discount'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Five-finger discount**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Golden opportunity** (सुनहरा अवसर): A very good chance to achieve something.

 
 
• **Example:** Getting a scholarship to study abroad is a golden opportunity for many students.
 
 
 
• **Green thumb** (पौधे उगाने की कला): Natural talent for growing plants.
 
 
• **Example:** My grandmother has a green thumb; her garden is always full of beautiful flowers.
 
 
 
• **Black sheep** (परिवार का बदनाम सदस्य): A person who is considered a disgrace to a particular group, usually a family.
 
 
• **Example:** He was considered the black sheep of the family due to his rebellious behavior.
 
 

152:Tc53,

The correct answer is: **Option 2.**
